identification.summary: AppMilad is described by Zimperium as an Iranian-based hacker group that used social media and Telegram to push users to sideload a fake app [S3]. Zimperium assesses that the actors behind the RatMilad Android spyware acquired the code from the AppMilad group and integrated it into a fake app [S2]. Coverage presents this as a hypothesis, and all sources found re-report one October 2022 Zimperium disclosure [S2].
identification.notes: AppMilad (a code source/ group) and the RatMilad operators (who used the code) are not established as the same entity; the link is Zimperium's belief .

attribution.confidence: Low. Zimperium states a belief, presented in coverage as a hypothesis; no government attribution found .
attribution.basis: Zimperium believes the RatMilad operators acquired code from AppMilad [S2]. No state sponsor is stated in the sources reviewed.

targeting.notes: Zimperium first saw RatMilad after a failed infection of a Middle East enterprise Android device protected by its software [S2]. Zimperium later assessed the RatMilad operators use a random-target approach, not a targeted campaign . Infection scale is unknown [S2].

capabilities.summary: RatMilad is Android spyware distributed outside app stores through links on social media and Telegram, tricking users into sideloading it and granting extensive permissions [S2][S3]. It was hidden in a VPN/phone-number spoofing app called Text Me, and a later live sample in NumRent, a renamed and graphically updated Text Me [S2][S3]. It can use the camera for pictures and video, record audio, get GPS location, view pictures, and collect SMS, call logs, contacts, SIM information and clipboard data, and read/write files [S2][S3][S4].

campaigns.name: RatMilad spyware disclosure (Text Me / NumRent)
campaigns.summary: Zimperium zLabs reported RatMilad after it failed to infect a Middle East enterprise device [S2]. Samples were found in Text Me and later NumRent, spread via Telegram and social media; a Telegram post had over 4,700 views and over 200 shares [S2][S4].

diamond.adversary: AppMilad, an Iranian-based group per Zimperium, supplier of code later used by the RatMilad operators, whose identity is unknown .
diamond.capability: RatMilad Android spyware (camera, audio, GPS, SMS, call logs, contacts, files) [S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Telegram channels/posts and social media links for distribution; sideloaded APKs, not app stores [S2][S3].
diamond.victim: Enterprise Android users in the Middle East; random-target approach per Zimperium [S2].
diamond.technology: Android devices; sideloaded apps masquerading as VPN/phone-number spoofing utilities [S2][S3].

gaps: Zimperium's original blog could not be opened in this research; findings rely on secondary coverage of it [S2].
No evidence found of a state sponsor, tasking, or relationship between AppMilad and the RatMilad operators beyond Zimperium's belief.
Infection count, victim identities, C2 infrastructure and IOCs not captured.
No reporting found on AppMilad activity after October 2022.
Vendor naming overlaps with other Iranian clusters were not found; none should be assumed.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Battlespace: personal and enterprise Android devices in the Middle East reachable via Telegram and social media [S2]. Threat: low-sophistication, random-target spyware distribution through sideloading [S2]. MLCOA: continued social-engineered distribution of repackaged utility apps (VPN, number spoofing) with data collection from camera, microphone, GPS and messages [S2][S3]. MDCOA: reuse of the code against selected enterprise or government personnel, which sources do not show. Candidate indicators: sideloaded apps named Text Me or NumRent, Telegram links promoting VPN/number apps, apps requesting camera, microphone, SMS and location permissions [S2][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: brief personnel deployed to the Middle East on sideloading risk and Telegram-delivered apps [S2][S3]. Authorities: mobile device management and BYOD restrictions fall to the owning command or enterprise; no cited source addresses authorities. Mission assurance: enforce app-store-only installation and mobile threat defense on devices handling mission data [S2]. Coordination: report suspected samples to the local cyber security service provider and share indicators with the mobile security vendor community.

provenance.importedSummary: AppMilad is an Iranian hacking group that has been identified as the source of a spyware campaign called RatMilad. This spyware is designed to silently infiltrate victims' devices and gather personal and corporate information, including private communications and photos. The group has been distributing the spyware through fake apps and targeting primarily Middle Eastern enterprises.
